preferences.text: Reuse the user-approved Sleepyhead logos stored in the brand canvas registry and approved-logos/2026-10-15 archive instead of searching online again. Use the saved transparent orange-and-charcoal primary logo, or transparent white-and-charcoal reverse logo according to the scene. BOTH versions retain charcoal head, closed-eye e lower halves and TM: the reverse is not an all-white logo. Ensure contrast for every colour; do not place charcoal on an equally dark background or white lettering on white. Preserve exact shapes, two-tone colouring, spacing, trademark and proportions; never redraw. Original background versions are archived; use transparent derivatives when placing on artwork.

Wardrobe for people in Sleepyhead scenes: young, playful, expressive at-home style that mixes loungewear and casual streetwear, never formal. One look per person: an oversized tee, hoodie, sweatshirt or knit sweater with joggers, cargo pants or wide-leg trousers; an overshirt over a white tee with chinos; a cami or tank with printed pyjama pants; a matching knit or striped lounge set; or a bold satin pyjama set. Colour: bright and pastel shades (pink, lilac, orange, rust, mustard, cobalt, sage) as one or two pops against cream, oatmeal, white or charcoal; calmer neutral sets suit sleep and rest moments. Playful prints are welcome (stripes, checks, daisies, tie-dye, waves), but no readable words, slogans or brand logos on clothes or shoes. Fun extras in moderation: headphones, hair clips, fun socks, a simple chain. Barefoot, socks, chunky sneakers or clogs; never shoes on a mattress or bedding. Relaxed, oversized fit; tasteful coverage.

Room look for Sleepyhead scenes: playful, colourful, lived-in Gen-Z homes, from warm and earthy to bold maximalist. Walls: colour-blocked paint (cobalt blue, blush or hot pink, terracotta, coral, mustard, lilac, peach, orange), often with arches, curves or stripes; warm walnut wood floors and furniture. Decor: playful rugs (checkerboard, wavy, geometric, confetti), Matisse-style abstract prints or a poster gallery wall, sculptural lamps (mushroom, globe, pleated paper), curvy mirrors, quirky ceramics, plants and trailing vines, books and personal touches (vinyl, headphones, skateboard, plush toy, home-workout gear). Light: bright sunny daylight, or a warm evening glow from LED strips, fairy lights or a neon shape (heart, wave, smiley). No readable words on signs, posters or walls, and no other brands. The product stays the hero: room colours complement it, the area right around it stays calmer, and no pattern or clutter hides or clashes with it.
